title: Quasi-two-dimensional Majorana zero modes from finite-size-coupled chiral hinge states
abstract: Majorana zero modes (MZMs) in topological superconductors have attracted broad research interest for their potential applications in topological quantum computation. In this work, we propose a quasi-two-dimensional route to realize spatially separated MZMs in a chiral higher-order topological insulator (HOTI) proximitized by a conventional $s$-wave superconductor through a theoretical model study. In three dimensions, the chiral HOTI hosts gapless hinge states along the $z$ direction, arising from a mass term that anisotropically gaps the surface Dirac cones of a topological insulator. By confining the sample along the $x$ direction while keeping it extended along $y$ and finite along $z$, opposite $z$-directed chiral hinge states hybridize and effectively form one-dimensional helical channels. Incorporating the superconducting proximity effect into this quasi-two-dimensional system induces effective $p$-wave pairing in these helical channels, thereby opening a topological gap. A fully open-boundary sample then hosts four localized MZMs, one at each endpoint of the helical channels, realizing a second-order topological superconductor characterized by Majorana corner modes. In addition to MZMs, we also find that superconducting pairing in this model produces extended Majorana hinge modes in three dimensions. Furthermore, representative disorder calculations indicate that these Majorana corner modes are robust against weak-to-moderate disorder, provided the excitation gap remains open. These results establish finite-size-coupled chiral hinge states as a promising platform for engineering multiple MZMs via conventional superconducting proximity effect.
summary: The paper presents a theoretical design to create multiple Majorana zero modes (MZMs) by coupling chiral hinge states from a higher-order topological insulator (HOTI) with an s-wave superconductor. By reducing the system dimensionality, opposite hinge states form helical channels, and superconducting pairing opens a gap, localizing four robust MZMs at the corners of the sample.
main_problem: The work proposes a theoretical route to realize spatially separated Majorana zero modes (MZMs) by exploiting the boundary physics of higher-order topological insulators (HOTIs). This is achieved through proximity coupling with an s-wave superconductor in a quasi-two-dimensional geometry.
main_result: The model successfully predicts the formation of four localized MZMs at the corners, characterizing the system as a second-order topological superconductor. These corner modes are shown to be robust against weak to moderate disorder.
method: The study employs theoretical modeling using the Bogoliubov-de-Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian and analyzes spectral properties under varying boundary conditions and disorder strengths.
model_or_system: The system is a chiral HOTI, which hosts gapless hinge states in 3D. By confining it quasi-2D, opposite chiral hinge states hybridize into helical channels. Superconducting proximity effect induces effective p-wave pairing on these channels, leading to the topological superconducting state.
key_observables: Zero-bias conductance peaks (STM signature), localized MZMs at corners, and the spectral gap opening in the BdG spectrum.
important_parameters: The confinement direction ($x$), the chemical potential ($\mu$) tuned into reconstructed hinge bands, and the superconducting pairing strength ($\Delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the chiral HOTI can be realized and that the proximity effect induces effective p-wave pairing. Robustness is confirmed only against weak-to-moderate disorder.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate gapless hinge states in 3D, the formation of helical channels upon confinement, and BdG spectra showing the emergence of four localized MZMs at the corners when tuned into the topological superconducting phase.
paper_structure: The paper builds from identifying gapless hinge states in a 3D HOTI to analyzing their hybridization in a quasi-2D geometry. The core mechanism involves proximity coupling inducing p-wave pairing, which opens a topological gap and localizes MZMs at the boundaries (corners). Disorder robustness is confirmed last.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, material-agnostic theoretical blueprint for engineering multiple MZMs using established superconducting techniques on advanced topological materials, bridging HOTI physics with superconductivity.

The sample is thin along x, extended along y, and finite along z. Oppo- site z-directed hinge states hybridize across the thin direction. The proximity-induced pairing gaps the two separated hinge- derived channels indicated by dashed red arrows. The four MZMs γ1,2,3,4 are localized at the endpoints of these channels in the y-z plane.
